extraction_warnings: This paper reports only study-level aggregate statistics (e.g., age range, % female, destination counts); no individual subject/sample-level identifiers or per-sample metadata (age, sex, DNA extraction kit, exact collection day) were available in the provided text.

Several schema fields (study_name, subject_id, sample_id, curator, pmid, dna_extraction_kit, target_condition, control) could not be populated because the paper does not explicitly provide this information in the given text; some details may exist in supplementary tables (e.g., Table S1-S4) not included here.
The 'age' field could not be expressed as a single number because only a range (23-34 years) was reported; age_group was derived from this range.
Sex was reported only as an aggregate percentage (74% female), which does not map to a single-subject enum value without fabricating sample-level data.

Two sequencing platforms were used in this study (Illumina HiSeq 2000 for metagenomic samples, Illumina MiSeq for ESBL isolate genomes); only the primary metagenomic platform (IlluminaHiSeq) was selected for the single-value field.

This paper is a metagenomic study of gut microbiome/antibiotic resistance genes in traveling students, so most schema fields (zygosity, neonatal, obgyn, tumor staging, disease response) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.

The 'disease' and 'disease_details' fields were inferred as 'Healthy' based on cohort description as exchange students, since no explicit disease/health status statement was found; confidence set to medium/low accordingly.

The 'treatment' field (antimalarial chemoprophylaxis) is reported at subgroup level (Central Africa vs Indian peninsula) even though overall granularity was set to study_level; see by_subgroup for details.

The 'feces_phenotype' field could not be confidently mapped to the schema's static ontology terms given available text, so it was marked not_reported despite fecal specimens being central to the study.

This paper is a microbiome/antibiotic resistance metagenomics study in healthy travelers, not a clinical oncology trial; most schema fields (biomarker, disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor_size) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.

feces_phenotype_value and uncurated_metadata fields were ambiguous given the schema's apparent clinical-trial orientation versus this microbiome study; conservatively marked not_reported to avoid fabrication.

Table 1 contains rich quantitative data on resistance gene abundances (fold changes, copies per 16S rRNA) before/after travel that could be relevant if biomarker fields are reinterpreted broadly, but were not extracted due to lack of explicit 'biomarker' framing in the source text.
